status: declared by the pull request that closes #445, before any score: the candidates, the features, the ridge setting, the fallback, the turning-point definition and the lag statistic below are fixed here and nothing is tuned on a scored day

scoring.note: scored days are before 2026-01-01 (docs/decisions/lockbox.md); the 2026 confirmation window is not looked at and no candidate here names it

admitted.on_rrp_sameday: the Desk's reverse-repo results for the scored row's own day, admitted for a day only when its records' lastUpdated is on the operation date at or before 15:00 New York time (nyfed_on_rrp_sameday in metadata/sources_measurement.json)
admitted.treasury_settlement: the day's gross Treasury settlement, a scheduled input already declared in metadata/sources.json (treasury_auctions.scheduled_availability: announced a panel day ahead, at 15:00)
admitted.last_published_spread: SOFR minus IORB of the day before the nowcast row, public at 15:00 on the nowcast row (nyfed_sofr.release_lag), with the spread of the day before that

excluded.treasury_bill_rates_sameday: no publication time before 16:00 New York time can be established: Treasury's page states the quotes are obtained at or near 3:30 PM and states no publication time, and the H.15 file is at 16:30 (metadata/sources_measurement.json, treasury_bill_rates_sameday)

nowcast.target: the spread of the nowcast row, SOFR - IORB in basis points, minus the spread of the row before it (the naive nowcast's error)
nowcast.row: the nowcast for row r is made at the decision instant of row r, 16:00 New York time, and is read by a forecast of day r + 1 (horizon 1) from row r
nowcast.estimator: ridge regression on standardized features, the intercept unpenalized, refitted every 21 rows from the first row with min_pairs usable pairs, on pairs (features of row k, target of row k) for k at most r - 1 only, expanding window
nowcast.fallback: the naive nowcast (the spread of the row before) on any row where the model is not yet fitted or a feature of the model is missing on the row or in a pair; the fallback is used and counted, never filled

feature_definitions.spread_prev_change_bp: spread of row r - 1 minus the spread of row r - 2, bp
feature_definitions.rrp_level_tn: same-day reverse repo accepted on row r, USD trillions
feature_definitions.rrp_change_tn: rrp_level_tn minus the same measure on row r - 1 (both must be admitted), USD trillions
feature_definitions.settlement_100bn: treasury_settlement on row r, in hundreds of USD billions
feature_definitions.quarter_end: the panel's quarter_end calendar column on row r
feature_definitions.tax_date: the panel's tax_date calendar column on row r
feature_definitions.month_end_window: 1 when the panel's days_to_month_end on row r is at most 2

naive.note: the spread of row r - 1, which is the latest published value

published_only.note: the ridge with the last published values alone: what mean reversion and momentum give without any same-day input

rrp_settlement.note: the nowcast that feeds the distribution model and the pressure classifier, fixed here and not chosen on any score

rrp_settlement_calendar.note: reported only: the calendar columns are always known, but the directive names the three inputs above, so this row says what the calendar adds

distribution.published: the published distribution of docs/runs/published_distribution_daily_h1.json: #169's gbm with nested conformal PID, the nine features of final_test_preregistration.CRPS_FEATURES, minimum history 61, refit every 21 scored days
distribution.variant: the same fitter, calibration, minimum history and refit cadence with one more feature, spread_nowcast_bps (the primary nowcast), and nothing else changed
distribution.baseline: as-of persistence, final_test_opening.distribution_walk on the persistence side of live_record._compare_sides(1)
distribution.score: crps_from_quantiles over the five quantiles, in basis points, the score of the published record

lag.statistic: the integer k in -3..5 at which the Pearson correlation of the forecast median of day T with the actual spread of day T - k is highest, over the scored days; the correlation at every k is reported
lag.paired: the interval is the 90% stationary-bootstrap interval of the difference in that k between a variant and the published model, resampling days jointly, and of the difference in correlation at k = 0 and k = 2

turning_points.definition: a scored day T is a turning point when the actual spread moves by at least minimum_move_bp into T and by at least minimum_move_bp the other way out of T: |s(T) - s(T-1)| >= m, |s(T+1) - s(T)| >= m and the two moves have opposite signs (a peak or a trough). The label uses the outcome of T + 1 and is a way of picking days to score, never an input of a forecast; a scored day whose T + 1 is after 2025-12-31 is not classified
turning_points.measure: the mean absolute error of the forecast median against the actual spread of T on these days and on the other days, paired between a variant and the published model, with the bootstrap interval above

pressure.variant_features: the nine features of published_v1 at the horizon plus spread_nowcast_bps, read at the row the as-of rule allows (row T - h)
pressure.verdicts: metadata/pressure_judge.json: tier 1 (onset warning), tier 3 (no crying wolf) and tier 5 (week ahead), at +5 bp, paired against the control with the judge's bootstrap

accuracy.paired: the per-day absolute error of a candidate minus the naive's, with the 90% stationary-bootstrap interval of the distribution block

amendment.made: 9 October 2026, by the pull request that closes #445, after the declared variant (the nowcast as one more regressor) and its pressure classifier were scored and before any score of the substituted variants below. The nowcast, its candidates, its ridge setting and its fallback are unchanged.
amendment.why: The published gbm is fitted on one-step pairs: the design row of a training target is the row before it, whatever lag the as-of rule gives each field when the model predicts (ml.fit_gradient_boosted_quantiles, training_pairs None). A regressor added to it is therefore learned at the same lag as the spread, and at prediction time is read one day fresher. An oracle column holding the nowcast row's own actual spread is, in every training pair, the spread regressor itself, so the fitted forecasts equal the published ones to the last digit; the declared variant cannot carry same-day information whatever the nowcast holds. The directive says the day-T forecast is built from the nowcast, so the substituted variant feeds the nowcast to the unchanged model as its latest spread.
amendment.substituted: The published model, fitted exactly as published (the nine features, one-step pairs on the actual spreads), and at prediction its feature row's spread is the primary nowcast of the row before the target instead of the published spread two rows before it. The nowcast column is declared to the as-of rule (so its read passes the leakage and staleness guards) and is not a regressor of the fitter. Nothing else changes.
amendment.checks: (1) The substituted variant fed the naive nowcast (nowcast_naive, the published spread itself) reproduces the published forecasts exactly. (2) An oracle ceiling, the substituted variant fed the nowcast row's own actual spread: inadmissible, reported only as the most that closing the lag could be worth, and never a candidate. (3) Under the declared variant the oracle reproduces the published forecasts exactly, which is the diagnosis above.
amendment.pressure_variant: published_v1_nowcast_substituted in metadata/pressure_judge.json: the same classifier, fed as the substituted distribution is
